credentials._note: IDs only. Secrets live in n8n, encrypted under N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Never store keys here.
credentials._credentialNote: n8n caches a credential's display name inside each node, so a renamed credential leaves stale labels behind and the ID is the only thing that means anything. This block used to map gBDmBd3jHGBqqQjl to 'Outlook - Dev (gtutor)'; that ID is in fact 'Outlook - Yancey', the production credential. WF-S's seeder inherited the mistake and was bound to Yancey's live mailbox while its sticky note promised dev-only. Use targets.<env>.outlookCredentialId.

published._note: Live state as of 2026-08-28. WF-A, WF-B, WF-C and WF-E are published and active in production.

_note: IDs only. Secrets live in n8n, encrypted under N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Never store keys here. There is deliberately no top-level workflows block: it duplicated the production ids and a missing id in a target silently fell back to it, which once had a dev build of WF-A calling the production WF-B. Every id is read from targets.<env>.workflows or the build fails.

prod.label: Yancey (live)
prod._digestToNote: Delivered by writing the message into the mailbox via Graph, not by email, so no verified domain is needed and Resend is out of the picture entirely. The POST targets /me, so the digest always lands in the mailbox the credential owns - digestTo is only the displayed To: header and cannot misroute it. digestFrom is the display identity and is listed in WF-A's ignoreSenders, so the agent does not classify its own digest.
prod._wfDNote: Attachment reading switched on in production on 2026-09-02 at the account owner's instruction. Yancey had previously been told in writing that attachments are never opened, so the Controls and Definitions doc was rewritten in the same pass to say what is read, what is not, and that PDFs and images are the only kinds that leave the server. Clearing this key is the whole off switch: WF-A only reads attachments when its target names a wfD.
prod._wfFNote: WF-F reviews the Task Management library: it categorises every document, checks each name against Yancey's convention, and reviews where each file sits. It rests with applyRenames false, so a run produces a review and changes nothing; arming it is a deliberate edit to the Config node and the cap limits one run to a handful of files. It proposes no moves at all - a move changes a path exactly as a rename changes a name, so it breaks a Power BI refresh the same way, and moving anything between the numbered stage folders would assert how far work has got, which no file records. Six renames were applied on 2026-09-02 after the plan was read; the record and the undo list are in fixtures/sharepoint/renames-applied.json and on the review page.

_sharepointNote: Phase 2, resolved 2026-09-02. The earlier 403s came from probing SharePoint with the *Outlook* credential, which proves nothing: the SharePoint node has its own credential type, microsoftSharePointOAuth2Api, targeting the SharePoint resource rather than Microsoft Graph. The permissions that matter live under Office 365 SharePoint Online (00000003-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000), not Graph Sites.*, on the same Entra app already used for Outlook. No new app and no admin were needed. Host is upperformpartners.sharepoint.com, not partnersperform. Writing was blocked because AllSites.Write sat unconsented while the credential asked for .default, which means 'whatever is already consented' and so hands back a weaker token in silence rather than an error - reconnecting changes nothing. Naming the scope explicitly forces the consent prompt. Do not press Grant admin consent on that page: it would also grant AllSites.FullControl, which is tenant-wide full control for a workflow that renames files.

policy._note: Yancey's drafting rules, 2026-08-28. Read by both wf-a-classify.mjs and scripts/golden-set.mjs so the gate cannot test a policy that is not the one deployed.
policy._confidenceNote: Yancey set confidenceMin to 0.80 on 2026-08-28, up from 0.60. Anything the classifier is less sure of than that is surfaced with below_confidence_min rather than replied to.

retention._note: Answering Yancey's question of 2026-08-28. n8n execution history — which holds full message bodies while a run is in flight — is pruned after 168 hours (7 days) by EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE and EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE on the VPS. The decision log (agent_email_log_yancey) holds subject, sender, label, reasoning and links, and is retained indefinitely so the audit trail survives; rows are closed after autoCloseDays but never deleted. Deleting a client's decision record is his call, not ours, so logRetentionDays defaults to 0 (never). Set it to a number of days to enable purging of closed rows.

_conventions._note: How the n8n instance is kept organised. Enforced by src/deployment.test.js where it can be, and by reading where it cannot.
_conventions.naming: Two classes of name, and the prefix says which. "WF-<letter> - Title" is a generated unit: the generator composes it as NAME + targets.<t>.nameSuffix, production keeps the bare name and dev adds " . dev". Never rename one of those in the n8n editor, because the next build renames it back. "Tool - Title" is hand-built and nothing rebuilds it; those are listed under diagnostics below. Sorting by name puts a unit beside its own dev copy, which is how you notice one has drifted.
_conventions.tags: Exactly one environment tag (prod | dev) and exactly one system tag (email-agent | documents) on every workflow, plus "diagnostic" on anything that must never be scheduled or left published. Production used to be identified only by the absence of a dev tag, which no filter can express. "phase-1" and "upperform" were removed: they were on every workflow and so selected nothing.
_conventions.archiving: Archive scaffolding once the answer it was built for is written down, and archive anything that would now give a wrong answer. But keep what creates test conditions: reading execution data replaced the helpers that inspected a run, and nothing replaces a seeder. Never archive a workflow the dev sandbox needs to exercise a path end to end.
_conventions.everything_is_generated: Every workflow that touches production is generated from workflows/*.mjs, and every WF- name is one of those. Hand-built tools are allowed where they create test conditions the generated workflows cannot, but they carry a Tool prefix, are tagged diagnostic, and must be listed under diagnostics below so the repo knows about every workflow in the instance.

diagnostics._note: Hand-run tools with no generator. Nothing rebuilds these, so a change to src/ does not reach them — which is fine for fixtures, and the reason they are named Tool rather than WF-.

seedAttachments.name: Tool · Seed Attachment Fixtures · dev
seedAttachments.why: WF-S seeds six plain messages and no attachments, so this is the only way to put one in front of WF-D in the sandbox.

seedPdfs.name: Tool · Seed PDF Fixtures · dev
seedPdfs.why: PDFs are one of only two kinds that leave the server for OpenAI, so the path most worth re-testing after any change to attachment handling.

sharepointPermissions.name: Tool · SharePoint Permissions (read-only)
sharepointPermissions.why: Reports the gap between what the token can do and what the person may do. When the second is wider, the OAuth scope is the limiter and no site permission will help.

diagnostics._folding: The two seeders overlap with wf-s-seed.mjs and would be better folded into it, so one generated seeder covers plain, Office and PDF fixtures. Not done: they work, and rebuilding a working seeder to save a row in a list is the wrong trade.
